path.data-label: Met: Spread opens the same notes as the cockpit for a project-os repository: the same list, the same statuses, checked side by side on this repository. **2026-09-06:** Deck draws this repository's thirty notes as cards, read through the sidecar the cockpit itself was using, so the payload is the same one by construction. **2026-09-07:** the comparison is now a real one rather than a formality. Deck draws the sidecar's own groups as headings with counts, keeps what is owed at the top, folds finished work away and lists a note's children under it, so the two applications can be read against each other heading by heading ([[TASK-0023-The-Groups-The-Sidecar-Sends-Are-Drawn]], [[TST-0016-The-Groups-The-Sidecar-Sends-Are-Drawn]]). The side-by-side comparison a person makes is [[TST-0008-Spread-Opens-The-Same-Notes-As-The-Cockpit]], reworded the same day for the navigator. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked it pass in the release ledger.

path.data-label: Met: A popped-out panel carrying one thing, which is the Needs-you strip, a single note, or a desk, sits on a second display and is still there carrying the same thing after Deck is restarted. **2026-09-07, built:** pop out now asks what the window should carry and the answer is one of three panels, the panel travels in the address, and a restart reopens the window carrying the same panel on the display it was left on ([[TASK-0026-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]], [[TST-0020-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]]). The walk needs a second monitor and is [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]], reworded the same day to name the status window again. **Restored 2026-09-07:** on 2026-09-06 this criterion was amended down to "a popped-out window", because Deck has no status panel and a pop-out is the same view again with no navigation. Edwin's decision on 2026-09-07 is that the application should be changed to match the criterion rather than the other way round, so the status window is back and [[TASK-0026-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]] builds it. **2026-09-06:** the placement half is built, and the decision is a pure function tested over display sets including an unplugged monitor ([[TST-0003-A-Window-Is-Placed-On-The-Display-It-Was-On]]). The walk needs a second monitor and is [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]], whose Procedure goes back to naming a status window when TASK-0026 lands. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]] pass in the release ledger.

path.data-label: Not yet met: Deck served over the local network opens in Safari on a tablet, reads the notes, and refuses every write at its own host. **2026-09-06:** the host is built and the refusal is tested over real HTTP, including methods a browser will not send; `--lan` binds it beyond loopback. The tablet itself is [[TST-0010-Deck-Opens-Read-Only-On-A-Tablet]]. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked it pass in the release ledger. **Reopened 2026-09-08:** that pass is invalidated in the ledger and the criterion is unticked, because the fixes of 2026-09-07 changed two things inside this claim — what a tablet gets while a sidecar is still indexing, and what Deck's host will forward. The check now walks both.

path.data-label: Met: Every row of the cockpit's capability register that Spread relies on is marked `adopted` in `docs/reference/cockpit-adoption.md`, with the register re-read on the day the phase closes. **Re-read 2026-09-07, the closing day:** the cockpit is still at commit `c0ed9e3` and has landed no change note since the previous read, so no key arrived and no row moved. The keys were compared mechanically rather than by eye: the register lists 55, [[REFERENCE-COCKPIT-ADOPTION]] carries 55, and neither side holds a key the other lacks. The nine rows Spread relies on — `surface.shell`, `shell.workspaces.rail`, `shell.workspaces.discovery`, `shell.nav.modes`, `shell.reader.render`, `shell.windows`, `api.read.nav`, `api.read.note` and `api.read.record` — are all `adopted`, as are `shell.nav.needs-you`, `shell.nav.hide-completed`, `shell.stage.find` and `api.guards`. The dated line is in that note's Maintenance section. **2026-09-06:** the register was read and twelve rows moved.

path.data-label: Met: **Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** The seven project-os views are seven descriptions and draw exactly what they draw today, checked against the fixture read off the cockpit's own navigator ([[TST-0006-Views-Come-From-The-Provider-And-Match-The-Cockpit]], [[TST-0030-A-Description-Parses-Or-Says-Why-Not]]). A difference that looks like an improvement is still a difference and still fails this criterion. **Evidence:** the fixture check is unedited and passes — the same seven ids and labels, in the cockpit's order. All seven parse with zero refusals, each naming `list` and `spread` and none naming `glass`. The smoke run drew the same two headings and the same thirteen rows before and after the change. The one thing the shape could not carry is Overview, which is a page of statistics rather than a view of notes; it is written in Deck's own extension namespace and the finding is in [[TASK-0042-Seven-Descriptions-Equal-To-Todays-Views]] rather than hidden in a workaround.
path.title: Met: **Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** The seven project-os views are seven descriptions and draw exactly what they draw today, checked against the fixture read off the cockpit's own navigator ([[TST-0006-Views-Come-From-The-Provider-And-Match-The-Cockpit]], [[TST-0030-A-Description-Parses-Or-Says-Why-Not]]). A difference that looks like an improvement is still a difference and still fails this criterion. **Evidence:** the fixture check is unedited and passes — the same seven ids and labels, in the cockpit's order. All seven parse with zero refusals, each naming `list` and `spread` and none naming `glass`. The smoke run drew the same two headings and the same thirteen rows before and after the change. The one thing the shape could not carry is Overview, which is a page of statistics rather than a view of notes; it is written in Deck's own extension namespace and the finding is in [[TASK-0042-Seven-Descriptions-Equal-To-Todays-Views]] rather than hidden in a workaround.

path.data-label: Not yet met: **Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the walk is owed.** A `.base` file from `~/Notes` reads as a Deck description, and every construct the evaluator does not support is named on screen — never an empty list with no explanation. Walked in [[TST-0027-A-Base-File-Reads-As-A-Description-And-The-Seven-Views-Are-Unchanged]] against three files of different shapes, including the TaskNotes plugin's own view types. **What is proved already:** all thirteen live base files — eleven from `~/Notes`, two from the cockpit's `docs/__bases__/` — read as descriptions, and every unsupported construct comes back named with its location. The TaskNotes plugin's four view types are reported without stopping the file. The unsupported report is drawn above the list rather than instead of it. **What is NOT proved:** that a vault's base file becomes a view a person can click, because the Vault PROVIDER is [[PHASE-0003-Vault]] and only the parser was built here. The walk is what says whether the parser half is enough to judge.

path.data-label: Not yet met: **Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the walk is owed.** A criterion ticked in Deck, with evidence, is ticked in the file and shows as ticked in the cockpit, and one status transition made in Deck moves the note's status the same way. Walked in [[TST-0028-A-Criterion-Ticked-In-Deck-Is-Ticked-In-The-Cockpit]] with `git diff` beside it, so the claim is about the file and not about two screens. **What is proved already:** both writes were made against the real sidecar this repository runs, on 2026-09-09, and reverted with `git checkout`. `ISS-0016` moved `triage` → `deferred` in the file with the sidecar's decision callout appended; a criterion was written as `- [x] … — evidence: … (actor, date)`, the sidecar's own `TICK_TEMPLATE`. **What is NOT proved and is why this stays unticked:** nobody has done it through Deck's own reader, with the cockpit open beside it, which is the half of the claim about two applications agreeing.

path.data-label: Not yet met: **Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the tablet walk is owed.** The served page offers no verb at all: not greyed out, absent. Checked on a real tablet in [[TST-0028-A-Criterion-Ticked-In-Deck-Is-Ticked-In-The-Cockpit]] and asserted in the smoke run, and Deck's host still answers 405 to every method that is not a read ([[ADR-0003-Deck-Writes-Through-The-Shell]]). **What is proved already:** the served host answers `write: false` and the shell answers `write: true`, both in the smoke run; the renderer's verbs sit behind that capability and the bridge they would use does not exist on a served page at all; and every method that is not `GET` or `HEAD` is refused 405 over real HTTP on seven paths, including the new records path and the two write paths. **What is NOT proved:** that a person looking at the page on a tablet sees nothing where a verb would be. That is a walk.

That is a walk.

path.data-label: Met: **Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** An address carrying the new keys — `surface`, `page`, `flow` and `step` — round-trips, and each key refuses a value it does not know. Every address that parsed before still parses to the same state, and an address naming an unregistered panel kind is refused until that kind is registered ([[TST-0034-The-Grammar-Carries-The-New-Keys-And-The-Panel-Registry-Refuses-Strangers]]). **Evidence:** 15 checks. The six round-trip states and the twelve malformed addresses moved into one file both suites read, so "nothing regressed" is a measurement over one table rather than over a copy of it, and the written form of an address with none of the new keys is byte-for-byte what it was. The load-bearing check refuses `?panel=acceptance-checks`, registers that kind, and parses the same address again.
path.title: Met: **Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** An address carrying the new keys — `surface`, `page`, `flow` and `step` — round-trips, and each key refuses a value it does not know. Every address that parsed before still parses to the same state, and an address naming an unregistered panel kind is refused until that kind is registered ([[TST-0034-The-Grammar-Carries-The-New-Keys-And-The-Panel-Registry-Refuses-Strangers]]). **Evidence:** 15 checks. The six round-trip states and the twelve malformed addresses moved into one file both suites read, so "nothing regressed" is a measurement over one table rather than over a copy of it, and the written form of an address with none of the new keys is byte-for-byte what it was. The load-bearing check refuses `?panel=acceptance-checks`, registers that kind, and parses the same address again.

The walk is Edwin's.

path.data-label: Not yet met: **Added 2026-09-10.** After a week of daily use in Glass, Edwin records from the compass how often he turned to look behind and whether anything was lost there. The DES-0002 review said this question should be a criterion rather than a remark, because the literature expects a "behind you" band to become a place things are forgotten, and pushing by hand makes that easier. Either answer is a result, and a bad one is what would retire the quiet band's placement, not the phase. Edwin's, after a week of use; nothing automated stands in for it.

path.data-label: Met: The frame time while turning is measured on the fleet's largest workspace in a foreground window and written as a number in [[FEAT-0009-The-Field-Where-Depth-Carries-Priority]], with the pooled-versus-canvas choice recorded beside it. If the number fails on a laptop, Spread returns to being the default and this note says so. Evidence, 2026-09-10: written in [[FEAT-0009-The-Field-Where-Depth-Carries-Priority]], "Measured": Your Trainer held the display's 16.7 ms median frame (17.0 ms at the 95th percentile) with two panes held and a reach drawn, 2.2 ms of script work per frame, 286 tiles and 2,303 elements at most, window in front; the hybrid is kept. Taken on a Mac Studio, not a laptop: the laptop reading is owed, and the throttled run (6.6 ms of work at 4× CPU cost) is an estimate.

path.data-label: Met: From the wheel, a phase, a ticket, a design, a release test check and a feature gate are each reached in at most two clicks, and by keyboard alone. Evidence: a sector opens its phase and a wedge its ticket (one click; TST-0093); on a ticket's screen its glyph opens its design, release test or gate (two clicks), and an owed-again badge opens the release test in one. Tab reaches every sector, disc and control, and the arrow keys and Enter reach and open all 361 and 2,747 tickets (Codex's round-two review of FEAT-0027).
